key_terms: When the source says an event happened, as opposed to ingestion time, when a pipeline accepted it, and processing time, when a computation handled it.
A window [a, b) that includes its start and excludes its end, so adjacent windows meet without counting a boundary event twice.
A rule that selects the version of each record known at a stated time, so a report can reproduce what was known then even after corrections arrive.
A revised value for an existing record that arrives after the original. It changes the current answer without changing the answer for an earlier as-of time.

worked_examples.title: Select a UTC day with a half-open interval
worked_examples.code:
from datetime import UTC, datetime

start = datetime(2026, 3, 1, tzinfo=UTC)
end = datetime(2026, 3, 2, tzinfo=UTC)
events = [
    datetime(2026, 2, 28, 23, 59, 59, tzinfo=UTC),
    datetime(2026, 3, 1, 0, 0, tzinfo=UTC),
    datetime(2026, 3, 1, 23, 59, 59, 999999, tzinfo=UTC),
    datetime(2026, 3, 2, 0, 0, tzinfo=UTC),
]
print([start <= t < end for t in events])
worked_examples.interpretation: Midnight on March 1 belongs to the day and midnight on March 2 belongs to the next one, so adjacent days never share or drop an event. A closed interval ending at 23:59:59 would lose the final microsecond of the day and a BETWEEN on both midnights would count the boundary twice. Check that both bounds are timezone-aware; mixing a naive bound with aware event times raises an error in Python and silently shifts rows in many SQL engines.

worked_examples.title: Keep the highest revision of each order
worked_examples.interpretation: Summing every row gives 19 because the corrected order is counted twice, while keeping the highest revision gives 15, which matches the corrected business fact. The sort makes the result independent of arrival order. If two rows share an order and revision with different amounts, this code keeps whichever sorts last, so a production version should reject that duplicate as a contract violation instead.

evidence: Complete actual local program with independent expected values and explicit negative checks; distributed-system claims are excluded.
